---
title: "02 - Batch Assessment and Correction"
subtitle: "Tissue source site effects in Prov-GigaPath embeddings"
format: html
editor: visual
---

Assesses and corrects tissue source site (TSS) batch effects in the slide
embeddings. TSS is nested within cancer type, so a pooled cross-cancer
correction cannot separate site from cancer biology. Correction is therefore
applied **within each cancer type**, and ComBat is compared with limma.

Inputs: `embed_raw_by_cancer.rds`, `meta_by_cancer.rds` (from 01)

Outputs: `embed_corrected_by_cancer.rds` (ComBat, used in 03 to 05),
`meta_corrected_by_cancer.rds` (adds `TSS.Grouped`),
`correction_diagnostics.rds`, figures in `figures/`

| Output | Content |
|---|---|
| Table 2.1 | Site is nested within cancer type |
| Table 2.2 | Site variance before and after correction, ComBat vs limma (main result) |
| Figure 2.1 | t-SNE before and after ComBat |
| Table S2.1 | Pooled correction removes cancer-type signal |
| Table S2.2 | Within-cancer site effects, all TCGA cancers |
| Table S2.3 | Sensitivity to the minimum site size |

## Libraries

```{r libraries, message=FALSE}
#| output: false
library(sva)        # ComBat
library(limma)      # removeBatchEffect (comparison method)
library(vegan)      # adonis2 (PERMANOVA)
library(vcd)        # assocstats (Cramer's V)
library(dplyr)      # data wrangling
library(ggplot2)    # figures
library(patchwork)  # combining panels
library(Rtsne)      # t-SNE
library(gt)         # tables
```

## Load data

```{r load}
data_dir <- "data"
fig_dir  <- "figures"
dir.create(fig_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)

embed_raw_by_cancer <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "embed_raw_by_cancer.rds"))  # patients x 768 per cancer
meta_by_cancer      <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "meta_by_cancer.rds"))       # metadata with TSS.Code

main_cancers <- c("KIRC", "COAD", "LUAD", "OV", "READ")  # carried forward to 03 to 05
all_cancers  <- names(embed_raw_by_cancer)               # used for supplementary tables

min_site_n <- 5      # sites with fewer patients are pooled into "other" before correction
set.seed(42)
```

## Helper functions

```{r helpers}
# Pool selected cancers into one matrix plus slim metadata (Patient, Cancer, TSS)
pool_cancers <- function(embed_list, meta_list, cancers) {
  embed_list <- embed_list[cancers]
  meta_list  <- meta_list[cancers]

  feats <- Reduce(intersect, lapply(embed_list, colnames))       # shared dimensions
  embed <- do.call(rbind, lapply(embed_list, function(m) m[, feats, drop = FALSE]))

  meta <- bind_rows(lapply(meta_list, function(m)
    data.frame(Patient = m$Patient, Cancer = m$Cancer,
               TSS.Code = m$TSS.Code, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)))
  rownames(meta) <- meta$Patient

  common <- intersect(rownames(embed), rownames(meta))           # align patients
  embed  <- embed[common, , drop = FALSE]
  meta   <- meta[common, , drop = FALSE]

  keep  <- complete.cases(meta$Cancer, meta$TSS.Code)            # guard against missing labels
  embed <- embed[keep, , drop = FALSE]
  meta  <- meta[keep, , drop = FALSE]

  meta$Cancer   <- droplevels(as.factor(meta$Cancer))
  meta$TSS.Code <- droplevels(as.factor(meta$TSS.Code))
  list(embed = embed, meta = meta)
}

# Pool sites with fewer than min_n patients into one "other" batch
collapse_sites <- function(meta, min_n) {
  tbl   <- table(meta$TSS.Code)                                  # patients per site
  small <- names(tbl[tbl < min_n])
  grp   <- as.character(meta$TSS.Code)
  grp[meta$TSS.Code %in% small] <- "other"
  droplevels(as.factor(grp))
}

# Standardise columns; constant columns would give NaN distances, so drop them
safe_scale <- function(mat) {
  sds  <- apply(mat, 2, sd, na.rm = TRUE)
  keep <- sds > 0 & !is.na(sds)
  if (sum(keep) < 2) return(NULL)
  scale(mat[, keep, drop = FALSE], center = TRUE, scale = TRUE)
}

# Total variance summed over all dimensions (unscaled)
total_var <- function(mat) sum(apply(mat, 2, var, na.rm = TRUE))
```

# Part A. Why correction must be done within cancer type

## Table 2.1 Nesting of site within cancer type

**Purpose:** shows that site and cancer type are confounded in TCGA.
**How to read:** a Cramer's V close to 1, with nearly all sites contributing
to a single cancer, means a pooled model cannot tell a site effect from a
cancer effect. All correction and testing is therefore done within each cancer.

```{r table2_1}
check_nesting <- function(cancers, label) {
  pooled <- pool_cancers(embed_raw_by_cancer, meta_by_cancer, cancers)
  tab    <- table(pooled$meta$TSS.Code, pooled$meta$Cancer)      # sites x cancers

  n_cancers_per_site <- apply(tab, 1, function(r) sum(r > 0))    # cancers each site contributes to
  cramer <- assocstats(table(pooled$meta$Cancer, pooled$meta$TSS.Code))$cramer

  data.frame(Cohort    = label,
             Patients  = nrow(pooled$meta),
             Sites     = nlevels(pooled$meta$TSS.Code),
             Pct_single_cancer_sites = round(100 * mean(n_cancers_per_site == 1), 1),
             Cramers_V = round(cramer, 3))                       # 1 = complete confounding
}

nesting_summary <- bind_rows(check_nesting(main_cancers, "Main 5 cancers"),
                             check_nesting(all_cancers,  "All cancers"))

nesting_summary %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(title = "Table 2.1 Tissue source site is nested within cancer type",
             subtitle = "Cramer's V of 1 indicates complete confounding") %>%
  cols_label(Pct_single_cancer_sites = "% sites in one cancer only", Cramers_V = "Cramer's V") %>%
  tab_options(table.font.size = 12, heading.align = "center")
```

## Pooled correction cannot protect cancer type

ComBat checks whether the covariate to protect (Cancer) is a combination of
the batch indicators. Because each site belongs to one cancer it is, so ComBat
rejects the model. **This error is the expected result.**

```{r pooled_fail}
pooled         <- pool_cancers(embed_raw_by_cancer, meta_by_cancer, main_cancers)
embed_t_pooled <- t(pooled$embed)                                # ComBat wants features x samples
design_cancer  <- model.matrix(~ Cancer, data = pooled$meta)     # Cancer as protected covariate

combat_protected <- tryCatch(
  ComBat(dat = embed_t_pooled, batch = pooled$meta$TSS.Code,
         mod = design_cancer, par.prior = TRUE, prior.plots = FALSE),
  error = function(e) {
    cat("ComBat rejected the Cancer-protected model:\n  ", conditionMessage(e), "\n"); NULL })
```

## Table S2.1 Pooled correction removes cancer-type signal

**Purpose:** shows what happens if the data are corrected in a pooled model anyway.
**How to read:** the only pooled model ComBat accepts does not protect Cancer,
so removing site means also removes cancer means. R2 Cancer should collapse
after pooled ComBat: the pooled approach erases real biology. In the Original
row, R2 TSS (entered after Cancer) is the site variance within cancer, which
Part B removes.

```{r tableS2_1}
combat_pooled <- ComBat(dat = embed_t_pooled, batch = pooled$meta$TSS.Code,
                        mod = NULL, par.prior = TRUE, prior.plots = FALSE)

pooled_mats <- list(Original = pooled$embed, `Pooled ComBat` = t(combat_pooled))

set.seed(42)
pooled_perm <- bind_rows(lapply(names(pooled_mats), function(nm) {
  s <- safe_scale(pooled_mats[[nm]])                             # standardise dimensions
  # Sequential terms with Cancer first: the TSS row is site variance within cancer
  r <- adonis2(dist(s) ~ Cancer + TSS.Code, data = pooled$meta,
               permutations = 999, by = "terms")
  data.frame(Method    = nm,
             R2_Cancer = r["Cancer", "R2"],   P_Cancer = r["Cancer", "Pr(>F)"],
             R2_TSS    = r["TSS.Code", "R2"], P_TSS    = r["TSS.Code", "Pr(>F)"])
}))

pooled_perm %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(title = "Table S2.1 Pooled correction removes cancer-type signal",
             subtitle = "PERMANOVA on the 5 pooled cancers; TSS entered after Cancer") %>%
  fmt_number(columns = starts_with("R2"), decimals = 3) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = starts_with("P_"), decimals = 3) %>%
  cols_label(R2_Cancer = "R2 Cancer", P_Cancer = "P Cancer",
             R2_TSS = "R2 TSS within cancer", P_TSS = "P TSS") %>%
  tab_options(table.font.size = 12, heading.align = "center")
```

# Part B. Within-cancer correction: ComBat versus limma

Cancer is constant within each subset, so no covariate needs protecting
(`mod = NULL`). Both methods remove site means. limma subtracts each observed
site mean exactly, so its site R2 is ~0 by construction. ComBat shrinks site
means towards the overall average (empirical Bayes), which matters when sites
are small. Overcorrection is therefore judged by **variance retained**: how
much of the original embedding variance survives correction.

```{r correct_fn}
correct_within_cancer <- function(cancer_label, embed_list, meta_list,
                                  min_n = min_site_n, n_perm = 999) {

  emb  <- embed_list[[cancer_label]]                             # patients x 768, raw
  meta <- meta_list[[cancer_label]]                              # patient metadata

  common <- intersect(rownames(emb), rownames(meta))             # align patients
  emb    <- emb[common, , drop = FALSE]
  meta   <- meta[common, , drop = FALSE]
  keep   <- !is.na(meta$TSS.Code)                                # guard against missing site
  emb    <- emb[keep, , drop = FALSE]
  meta   <- meta[keep, , drop = FALSE]

  meta$TSS.Code    <- droplevels(as.factor(meta$TSS.Code))       # every real site
  meta$TSS.Grouped <- collapse_sites(meta, min_n)                # small sites pooled into "other"

  if (nlevels(meta$TSS.Grouped) < 2 || nrow(emb) < 10) {         # nothing to correct
    cat(cancer_label, ": insufficient site diversity or n, skipping\n")
    return(NULL)
  }

  embed_t <- t(emb)                                              # features x patients
  batch   <- meta$TSS.Grouped

  # ComBat: empirical Bayes shrinkage of site means and variances
  combat <- tryCatch(
    ComBat(dat = embed_t, batch = batch, mod = NULL, par.prior = TRUE, prior.plots = FALSE),
    error = function(e) { cat(cancer_label, "ComBat failed:", conditionMessage(e), "\n"); NULL })

  # limma: exact subtraction of observed site means
  lmm <- tryCatch(
    removeBatchEffect(x = embed_t, batch = batch),
    error = function(e) { cat(cancer_label, "limma failed:", conditionMessage(e), "\n"); NULL })

  if (is.null(combat) || is.null(lmm)) return(NULL)

  emb_combat <- t(combat); rownames(emb_combat) <- rownames(emb) # back to patients x features
  emb_limma  <- t(lmm);    rownames(emb_limma)  <- rownames(emb)

  # Standardised versions for the PERMANOVA distances
  s_orig   <- safe_scale(emb)
  s_combat <- safe_scale(emb_combat)
  s_limma  <- safe_scale(emb_limma)
  if (is.null(s_orig) || is.null(s_combat) || is.null(s_limma)) {
    cat(cancer_label, ": no usable variance after filtering, skipping\n")
    return(NULL)
  }

  # PERMANOVA of site; resetting the seed gives identical permutations for each version
  set.seed(42)
  r_orig   <- adonis2(dist(s_orig)   ~ TSS.Grouped, data = meta, permutations = n_perm, by = "terms")
  set.seed(42)
  r_combat <- adonis2(dist(s_combat) ~ TSS.Grouped, data = meta, permutations = n_perm, by = "terms")
  set.seed(42)
  r_limma  <- adonis2(dist(s_limma)  ~ TSS.Grouped, data = meta, permutations = n_perm, by = "terms")

  v0     <- total_var(emb)                                       # raw variance (denominator)
  n_site <- table(meta$TSS.Code)                                 # patients per real site

  diagnostics <- data.frame(
    Cancer          = cancer_label,
    n_patients      = nrow(emb),
    n_sites_raw     = length(n_site),                            # real sites
    n_sites_small   = sum(n_site < min_n),                       # sites pooled into "other"
    n_sites_used    = nlevels(batch),                            # batches passed to ComBat/limma
    mean_only       = any(table(batch) == 1),                    # ComBat goes mean-only if a batch has n = 1
    R2_null         = (nlevels(batch) - 1) / (nrow(emb) - 1),    # expected site R2 with no site effect
    R2_TSS_orig     = r_orig["TSS.Grouped", "R2"],
    P_TSS_orig      = r_orig["TSS.Grouped", "Pr(>F)"],
    R2_TSS_combat   = r_combat["TSS.Grouped", "R2"],
    P_TSS_combat    = r_combat["TSS.Grouped", "Pr(>F)"],
    R2_TSS_limma    = r_limma["TSS.Grouped", "R2"],
    Var_kept_combat = total_var(emb_combat) / v0,                # share of raw variance retained
    Var_kept_limma  = total_var(emb_limma)  / v0)

  list(embed_combat = emb_combat, embed_limma = emb_limma,
       embed_raw = emb, meta = meta, diagnostics = diagnostics)
}
```

```{r run_correction}
# Every cancer is corrected for Table S2.2; the main 5 are carried forward
correction_all <- list()
for (cc in all_cancers) {
  cat("Correcting", cc, "\n")
  res <- tryCatch(correct_within_cancer(cc, embed_raw_by_cancer, meta_by_cancer),
                  error = function(e) { cat("  failed:", conditionMessage(e), "\n"); NULL })
  if (!is.null(res)) correction_all[[cc]] <- res
}

diag_all        <- bind_rows(lapply(correction_all, `[[`, "diagnostics"))          # all cancers
correction_list <- correction_all[intersect(main_cancers, names(correction_all))]  # main cohort
correction_diag <- filter(diag_all, Cancer %in% main_cancers)                      # Table 2.2

cat("Corrected:", length(correction_all), "cancers; main cohort:",
    paste(names(correction_list), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

## Table 2.2 Site variance before and after correction

**Purpose:** the main batch-effect result, one row per cancer.
**How to read, in three steps:**

1. Raw R2 well above the null expectation, with a small P, means site effects
   are present within each cancer.
2. ComBat R2 near the null means ComBat removed them.
3. limma retaining less variance than ComBat, especially where many sites are
   small, means limma removes patient signal along with the site means
   (overcorrection).

```{r table2_2}
correction_diag %>%
  select(Cancer, n_patients, n_sites_raw, n_sites_small, R2_null,
         R2_TSS_orig, P_TSS_orig, R2_TSS_combat, P_TSS_combat, R2_TSS_limma,
         Var_kept_combat, Var_kept_limma) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(title = "Table 2.2 Tissue source site variance before and after within-cancer correction",
             subtitle = paste0("PERMANOVA within each cancer; sites with n < ", min_site_n, " pooled")) %>%
  tab_spanner(label = "Sites", columns = c(n_sites_raw, n_sites_small)) %>%
  tab_spanner(label = "Site R2 (PERMANOVA)",
              columns = c(R2_null, R2_TSS_orig, P_TSS_orig, R2_TSS_combat, P_TSS_combat, R2_TSS_limma)) %>%
  tab_spanner(label = "Variance retained", columns = c(Var_kept_combat, Var_kept_limma)) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = starts_with("R2"), decimals = 3) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = starts_with("P_"), decimals = 3) %>%
  fmt_percent(columns = starts_with("Var_kept"), decimals = 1) %>%
  cols_label(n_patients = "Patients", n_sites_raw = "Total", n_sites_small = paste0("n < ", min_site_n),
             R2_null = "Expected (null)", R2_TSS_orig = "Raw", P_TSS_orig = "P",
             R2_TSS_combat = "ComBat", P_TSS_combat = "P", R2_TSS_limma = "limma",
             Var_kept_combat = "ComBat", Var_kept_limma = "limma") %>%
  tab_footnote(paste("Expected (null) = (sites - 1) / (patients - 1), the R2 expected with no site effect.",
                     "limma removes site means exactly, so its R2 is ~0 by construction;",
                     "overcorrection is judged by variance retained.")) %>%
  tab_options(table.font.size = 12, heading.align = "center")
```

## Figure 2.1 Embeddings before and after correction

**Purpose:** the visual counterpart of Table 2.2. **How to read:** colour is
cancer type, shape marks the three largest sites within each cancer. In Raw,
points of the same colour and shape bunch together inside their cancer's
cluster: that is the site effect. After ComBat, the shapes should be mixed
within each cluster, while the cancer clusters themselves stay separate,
because correction never crosses cancer types.

```{r fig2_1, fig.width=11, fig.height=5.5}
feats <- Reduce(intersect, lapply(correction_list, function(x) colnames(x$embed_raw)))  # shared dims

# Stack the per-cancer matrices; list order matches meta_stack below
stack_version <- function(slot)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(correction_list, function(x) x[[slot]][, feats, drop = FALSE]))

meta_stack <- bind_rows(lapply(correction_list, function(x)
  data.frame(Patient = rownames(x$meta), Cancer = x$meta$Cancer,
             TSS = as.character(x$meta$TSS.Grouped), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)))

versions <- list(`Raw embedding`    = stack_version("embed_raw"),
                 `ComBat-corrected` = stack_version("embed_combat"))

tsne_df <- bind_rows(lapply(names(versions), function(nm) {
  set.seed(42)                                                   # same seed for both versions
  ts <- Rtsne(as.matrix(versions[[nm]]), dims = 2, perplexity = 30,
              check_duplicates = FALSE, pca = TRUE)
  data.frame(TSNE1 = ts$Y[, 1], TSNE2 = ts$Y[, 2],
             Cancer = meta_stack$Cancer, TSS = meta_stack$TSS,
             Version = factor(nm, levels = names(versions)))
}))

# Sites are nested in cancers, so shapes are assigned within each cancer:
# the three largest real sites per cancer get a shape, the rest share one
rank_lab <- c("Largest site", "2nd largest", "3rd largest")
site_rank <- meta_stack %>%
  filter(TSS != "other") %>%                                     # pooled small sites are not one site
  dplyr::count(Cancer, TSS) %>%
  group_by(Cancer) %>%
  slice_max(n, n = 3, with_ties = FALSE) %>%                     # sorted largest first
  mutate(Site_rank = rank_lab[row_number()]) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(Cancer, TSS, Site_rank)

tsne_df <- tsne_df %>%
  left_join(site_rank, by = c("Cancer", "TSS")) %>%
  mutate(Site_rank = factor(ifelse(is.na(Site_rank), "Other sites", Site_rank),
                            levels = c(rank_lab, "Other sites")),
         Cancer    = factor(Cancer, levels = main_cancers))
tsne_df <- tsne_df[order(tsne_df$Site_rank != "Other sites"), ]  # other sites drawn first, underneath

# Cancer colours: Dark2, the palette used for views in 05
cancer_cols <- c(KIRC = "#1b9e77", COAD = "#d95f02", LUAD = "#7570b3",
                 OV   = "#e7298a", READ = "#66a61e")

others <- filter(tsne_df, Site_rank == "Other sites")                     # background layer
tops   <- filter(tsne_df, Site_rank != "Other sites") %>%                 # foreground layer
  mutate(Site_rank = droplevels(Site_rank))

fig2_1 <- ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = others, aes(TSNE1, TSNE2, colour = Cancer),
             size = 0.6, alpha = 0.3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_point(data = tops, aes(TSNE1, TSNE2, fill = Cancer, shape = Site_rank),
             size = 1.9, colour = "white", stroke = 0.2, alpha = 0.9) +   # white edge keeps points apart
  facet_wrap(~ Version, nrow = 1, scales = "free") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cancer_cols, guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cancer_cols, name = "Cancer type") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(24, 22, 23), name = "Site (within cancer)") +   # fillable ▲ ■ ◆
  guides(fill  = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = 21, size = 3.5)),
         shape = guide_legend(override.aes = list(fill = "grey40", size = 3))) +
  labs(title = "Figure 2.1 Prov-GigaPath embeddings before and after within-cancer ComBat",
       subtitle = "Shapes: three largest sites within each cancer; small dots: all other sites",
       x = "t-SNE 1", y = "t-SNE 2") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95", colour = NA),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
        legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "horizontal")

fig2_1
ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "Fig2_1_tSNE.pdf"), fig2_1, width = 11, height = 5.5)
```




## Table S2.2 Site effects across all TCGA cancer types

**Purpose:** shows whether site effects are specific to the main five cancers
or a general property of the embedding.
**How to read:** count the cancers with raw P < 0.05. If most are significant,
the site effect is pervasive, supporting correction in any use of these
embeddings. The variance-retained columns show whether the limma gap holds
across cancers.

```{r tableS2_2}
diag_all %>%
  arrange(desc(R2_TSS_orig - R2_null)) %>%                       # largest excess site signal first
  select(Cancer, n_patients, n_sites_raw, n_sites_small, R2_null, R2_TSS_orig, P_TSS_orig,
         R2_TSS_combat, Var_kept_combat, Var_kept_limma) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(title = "Table S2.2 Within-cancer site effects across all TCGA cancer types",
             subtitle = paste0("Sites with n < ", min_site_n, " pooled")) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = starts_with("R2"), decimals = 3) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = P_TSS_orig, decimals = 3) %>%
  fmt_percent(columns = starts_with("Var_kept"), decimals = 1) %>%
  cols_label(n_patients = "Patients", n_sites_raw = "Sites", n_sites_small = paste0("Sites n < ", min_site_n),
             R2_null = "R2 null", R2_TSS_orig = "R2 raw", P_TSS_orig = "P raw",
             R2_TSS_combat = "R2 ComBat", Var_kept_combat = "Var kept ComBat",
             Var_kept_limma = "Var kept limma") %>%
  tab_options(table.font.size = 11, heading.align = "center")
```

## Table S2.3 Sensitivity to the minimum site size

**Purpose:** directly tests whether small sites drive limma's overcorrection.
**How to read:** with no pooling ("n < 1", singleton sites kept), limma should
retain much less variance than ComBat, because it sets every patient at a
singleton site to the site mean. The gap should narrow as more small sites are
pooled. ComBat should be stable across thresholds, supporting the choice of
ComBat and of the 5-patient threshold.

```{r tableS2_3}
sens <- bind_rows(lapply(c(1, 3, 5, 10), function(mn) {
  bind_rows(lapply(main_cancers, function(cc) {
    r <- correct_within_cancer(cc, embed_raw_by_cancer, meta_by_cancer,
                               min_n = mn, n_perm = 99)          # fewer permutations: R2 is unaffected
    if (is.null(r)) return(NULL)
    r$diagnostics %>%
      mutate(Threshold = paste0("Sites with n < ", mn, " pooled")) %>%
      select(Threshold, Cancer, n_sites_used, mean_only,
             R2_TSS_orig, R2_TSS_combat, Var_kept_combat, Var_kept_limma)
  }))
}))

sens %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "Threshold") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Table S2.3 Effect of the minimum site size threshold",
             subtitle = "A larger gap in variance retained indicates limma overcorrection") %>%
  fmt_number(columns = starts_with("R2"), decimals = 3) %>%
  fmt_percent(columns = starts_with("Var_kept"), decimals = 1) %>%
  cols_label(n_sites_used = "Batches", mean_only = "ComBat mean-only",
             R2_TSS_orig = "R2 raw", R2_TSS_combat = "R2 ComBat",
             Var_kept_combat = "Var kept ComBat", Var_kept_limma = "Var kept limma") %>%
  tab_options(table.font.size = 11, heading.align = "center")
```

## Save corrected embeddings

ComBat-corrected embeddings for the main cohort are carried forward to 03 to 05.
The limma output is used only for the comparison above.

```{r save}
embed_corrected_by_cancer <- lapply(correction_list, `[[`, "embed_combat")  # patients x 768
meta_corrected_by_cancer  <- lapply(correction_list, `[[`, "meta")          # includes TSS.Grouped

saveRDS(embed_corrected_by_cancer, file.path(data_dir, "embed_corrected_by_cancer.rds"))
saveRDS(meta_corrected_by_cancer,  file.path(data_dir, "meta_corrected_by_cancer.rds"))
saveRDS(diag_all,                  file.path(data_dir, "correction_diagnostics.rds"))

cat("Saved:", paste(names(embed_corrected_by_cancer), collapse = ", "), "|",
    sum(sapply(embed_corrected_by_cancer, nrow)), "patients\n")
```

sessionInfo()
